questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Security Principles & Network Defense Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why does setting `rejectUnauthorized: false` during HTTPS requests create a severe vulnerability?

options.text: It skips certificate validation so an active MITM attacker presenting any bogus certificate can intercept and modify encrypted traffic unnoticed
It prevents HTTP POST bodies from being parsed
It slows network round trips by 10x
It deletes client session cookies automatically

questions.explanation: Encryption without server identity verification fails to stop active MITM proxies.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Security Principles & Network Defense Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What happens under a Stateful Inspection Firewall when a client initiates an outbound HTTPS session on port 443?

options.text: The firewall logs connection state in a state table and permits established return packets back cleanly without opening port 443 inbound globally
It leaves port 443 permanently open to unsolicited internet traffic
It drops all return traffic automatically
It scans user passwords in plaintext

questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls track active flows and distinguish return responses from unsolicited inbound scans.

questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Network Defense: Firewalls, Stateful Inspection & TLS 1.3

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Security Principles & Network Defense Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What security benefit does HSTS (`Strict-Transport-Security`) provide?

options.text: Instructs compliant browsers never to downgrade subsequent visits to insecure plaintext HTTP

questions.explanation: HSTS protects users against SSL-stripping downgrade attacks.
